messages:
amy_marketing: Heads-up — Ops flagged a partial degradation for the hosted API in eu-west. I want to align on customer-facing wording + timing before we publish. Quick sync here.

incident-bot: Incident detected: partial_degradation hosted-api eu-west — created at 2026-03-21T12:04:xxZ — Severity: S2

jason_ops: Thanks. We're seeing increased 5xxs on inference endpoints behind a single AZ. Mitigations in flight (route failover). ETA update in ~10–15m.

amy_marketing: Suggested initial status page line: `Investigating: Customers may experience intermittent 5xx errors for hosted inference in eu-west. Engineers are investigating.` Short, clear, no technical blame. Thoughts?

emily_support: That phrasing works. We should add a short note for customers with SLAs: "We are monitoring and will update within 15 minutes." Also prep an FAQ snippet for common troubleshooting steps (none on customer side right now).

rohan_eng: Agree with the short line. Small ask: add a separate internal note (not public) about request routing and impacted model families so Support can triage.

amy_marketing: Noted. Public copy v1 below — want feedback before I post to statuspage and schedule social/ops notifications: `Current status: Investigating — Intermittent 5xx errors affecting hosted inference in eu-west. We are rerouting traffic and will post updates within 15 minutes. No action required from customers at this time.`

jason_ops: 👍 Good. For cadence: publish initial at t+5 (now), follow-up at t+15 with impact scope, then a follow-up at t+60 or when a fix is shipped. If rollback or failover happens earlier, we post an update immediately.

emily_support: I'll prepare a Canned Response for affected customers: short apology, what we're doing, ETA for next update. Want to triage all in-product errors to a single support tag `#eu-west-5xx`.

nina_legal: Quick compliance check — if PII was in flight, we need to avoid phrases that imply data loss. The current wording is fine. If the impact changes to "data access" or "data loss" loop Legal back in before publishing.

amy_marketing: Good catch, Nina. We'll avoid any data language. Also, can someone confirm whether translations are needed for the status page? We should push an English initial update and queue translations if the incident lasts >30m.

jason_ops: Confirm translations only after 30 minutes or once we know a sustained impact. Ops will post the canonical English update. Marketing to push social copy and support copy after the first update lands.

amy_marketing: Plan of record: 1) Amy posts initial status (english) at t+5 — use public copy v1. 2) Ops posts technical follow-up at t+15 with scope & mitigation. 3) Marketing posts customer email draft and social copy after t+15. 4) Support pushes canned responses and in-product tag. 5) Legal on standby if wording shifts. Assign owners: amy_marketing (status copy + social), jason_ops (technical follow-ups), emily_support (canned responses), rohan_eng (internal technical triage), nina_legal (review).

rohan_eng: I'll add the internal impact note to the incident doc now (models: redwood-3b variants, affected AZ: eu-west-1b).

emily_support: Adding canned responses to Support repo and creating the `#eu-west-5xx` tag. Will notify CS leads.

amy_marketing: I'll publish the initial status now. Will follow up in-thread with the statuspage link. :thumbsup:

amy_marketing: (posted) https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rdw-2026-031 — initial update live.

emily_support: Saw it. Sending the first customer batch for impacted orgs in the next 10m.

jason_ops: Monitoring. If reroute completes, we'll update immediately with "Reduced error rate, monitoring". If not, next major update at t+60.

amy_marketing: Thanks everyone — will coordinate post-incident recap and suggested messaging for the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident rdw-2026-031 updated: status=investigating -> status=monitoring at 2026-03-21T12:37:xxZ
